global.faq.heading: Questions patients ask
global.faq.items.0.question: What does Medsafar charge me?
global.faq.items.0.answer: Nothing for the treatment plan and the cost estimate. You pay the hospital for treatment and the usual costs of travel and stay. Anything Medsafar charges is written down before you agree to it.
global.faq.items.1.question: Why is there no price on this page?
global.faq.items.1.answer: Because a real figure depends on your reports, the hospital and the length of stay. Where a hospital has given us its package prices, they are on that hospital's page as a guide. Either way, we send you a written estimate prepared for your case.
global.faq.items.2.question: Is Medsafar a hospital?
global.faq.items.2.answer: No. Medsafar is a medical travel facilitator. Treatment is given by independent hospitals and doctors in India. We arrange everything around it.
global.faq.items.3.question: Which reports should I send?
global.faq.items.3.answer: Whatever you already have: the doctor's letter, scans, blood test results or a discharge summary. Clear photos taken on a phone are fine.
global.faq.items.4.question: How soon will someone reply?
global.faq.items.4.answer: A case manager picks up your enquiry and comes back to you on WhatsApp or by call. A doctor's opinion takes longer, because a specialist has to read the reports.
global.faq.items.5.question: How many days will I spend in India?
global.faq.items.5.answer: That depends on what you need. A check-up or a minor procedure may take only a few days. A major operation, such as a knee or hip replacement, usually means two to three weeks, so you can recover before the flight home. Your treatment plan tells you what to expect.
global.faq.items.6.question: Can a family member travel with me?
global.faq.items.6.answer: Yes, and it helps to have someone with you. Indian medical visas allow attendants, so we add them to the visa invitation and arrange a room for them near the hospital.
global.faq.items.7.question: How does paying for treatment work?
global.faq.items.7.answer: You pay the hospital, based on the written estimate it gives you. Some hospitals take a small deposit to confirm your admission, and the balance is paid after you arrive. We go through every amount with you beforehand.
global.faq.items.8.question: Does Medsafar help after I return home?
global.faq.items.8.answer: Yes. We arrange follow-up calls with your doctor, share your reports with your local doctor if you want, and stay in touch while you recover.
global.faq.items.9.question: What happens to my medical reports?
global.faq.items.9.answer: They go to the doctors and hospitals reviewing your case, and nowhere else. You tick a box to allow that before we share anything.

catalog.treatments.detail.cost.intro: Every patient gets their own estimate, in writing, from the hospital. These are the things that move it.
catalog.treatments.detail.cost.factors.0: Room types, equipment and running costs differ from one hospital to the next.

catalog.treatments.detail.cost.factors.2: Keyhole or robotic surgery, and the make of any implant, can change the price.
catalog.treatments.detail.cost.factors.3: Other conditions, earlier treatment and the tests you need before treatment all count.
catalog.treatments.detail.cost.factors.4: Days in hospital, any time in intensive care and the weeks you spend recovering in India.
catalog.treatments.detail.cost.factors.5: Physiotherapy, medicines to take home and follow-up visits are added only if your doctor asks for them.

about.who.heading: Who we are
about.who.body.0: Medsafar helps people who live outside India get high-quality medical care in India at a fair price. We connect each patient with experienced doctors, surgeons and multi-speciality hospitals, and we take care of everything around the treatment so the patient and their family can focus on getting better.
about.who.body.1: Medsafar India is a division of Travgrub Private Limited, a travel company based in Mumbai. That is why we handle the travel side ourselves: the visa invitation, flights, airport pickup and a place to stay.

about.founder.picture.alt: Vicky Prabhu, founder and CEO of Medsafar
about.founder.quote.text: Medsafar exists to turn my lifelong desire to serve humanity into action: helping patients find the care they need, and bringing hope to families in their most difficult moments.
about.founder.story.heading: Why I started Medsafar
about.founder.story.body.0: I have always wanted to do something meaningful for people. My years with Rotary showed me that even a small act of kindness can make a real difference in someone's life.
about.founder.story.body.1: Running Travgrub taught me that travel is about people, not tickets. Visa help, an airport pickup, a place to stay, someone to call when you need help: small details that bring real peace of mind in a country you do not know.
about.founder.story.body.2: When someone falls seriously ill, the whole family carries the fear. Medsafar puts my travel experience to its most meaningful use: standing beside patients and their families, so they never feel alone.
about.founder.contact.body: Medsafar is small on purpose. Vicky looks after every patient himself, from the first message to the follow-up at home.

contact.why.items.2.title: One team, start to finish
contact.why.items.2.body: From the first message to your follow-up at home, one case manager looks after you and your family.
contact.faq.heading: Before you get in touch
contact.faq.items.0.question: Do I pay anything to get a treatment plan?
contact.faq.items.0.answer: No. The doctor's opinion, the treatment plan and the cost estimate are free, and you are under no obligation to go ahead.
contact.faq.items.1.question: How long will I need to stay in India?
contact.faq.items.1.answer: It depends on the treatment. Tests and small procedures can take a few days. Bigger operations, such as a joint replacement, usually mean two to three weeks, including time to recover before you fly home. Your plan gives a likely length of stay.
contact.faq.items.2.question: Can someone come with me?
contact.faq.items.2.answer: Yes, and we recommend it. A relative or friend can travel as your attendant. We include them in the visa invitation and find a room for them close to the hospital.
contact.faq.items.3.question: How do I pay for treatment?
contact.faq.items.3.answer: You pay the hospital directly, against its written estimate. Some hospitals ask for a small deposit to book your admission, with the rest settled when you arrive. Nothing is hidden, and we explain every amount first.
contact.faq.items.4.question: What happens after I go home?
contact.faq.items.4.answer: We stay in touch. We set up follow-up calls with your doctor, pass on your reports, and help with anything you need while you recover.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what Medsafar collects when you ask for help, why, who sees it and what you can ask us to do with it.
privacy.updated.label: Last updated
privacy.sections.0.heading: Who we are
privacy.sections.0.body: Medsafar India is a division of Travgrub Private Limited, registered office Office No. 222, 2nd Floor, NEO Corporate Plaza, Ramchandra Lane, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400064, India. We decide how your personal data is used, so under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 we are responsible for it.
privacy.sections.1.heading: What we collect
privacy.sections.1.body.0: What you give us: your mobile number, name, email, the country you live in, the treatment you need, when you want to travel, anything you write to the doctor, and any medical reports you upload or send us.
privacy.sections.1.body.1: If you go ahead with treatment, we also collect what the hospital and the visa need: your passport details, your travel dates, and the names of anyone travelling with you.
privacy.sections.1.body.2: What we collect automatically: a scrambled code made from your internet address, kept only to stop the enquiry form being misused. It cannot be turned back into the address. We also count visits to the site, without cookies and without identifying you.
privacy.sections.2.heading: How we use it
privacy.sections.2.body.0: To answer your enquiry, get a doctor's opinion and a written estimate, and arrange your treatment, visa, travel, stay and follow-up care.
privacy.sections.2.body.1: To contact you about your case by WhatsApp, phone or email.
privacy.sections.2.body.2: To keep the site working and safe, and to meet our legal duties.
privacy.sections.2.body.3: We do not sell your data, and we use your medical reports only for your own care.
privacy.sections.3.heading: Your consent
privacy.sections.3.body: When you send the enquiry form you agree that we may use your details and share your reports with partner hospitals and doctors in India to prepare your treatment plan. You can withdraw that consent at any time by writing to us. It does not undo what is already done, but we stop from then on.
privacy.sections.4.heading: Medical reports
privacy.sections.4.body: Health information is the most sensitive data you give us. Only the people working on your case see it: our case managers and the doctors and hospitals asked to plan your treatment. We store reports with our hosting provider, Cloudflare, under strict access control.
privacy.sections.5.heading: Who we share it with
privacy.sections.5.body.0: Partner hospitals and doctors in India, to plan and give your treatment.
privacy.sections.5.body.1: Airlines, hotels and visa services, only what they need to book your travel and stay. Travel may be booked through Travgrub Private Limited, our parent company.
privacy.sections.5.body.2: Your insurer, if you ask us to deal with them for you.
privacy.sections.5.body.3: Companies that run services for us, such as hosting (Cloudflare), messaging (WhatsApp) and email, under their own privacy duties.
privacy.sections.5.body.4: Government authorities, when the law requires it.
privacy.sections.6.heading: Data outside India
privacy.sections.6.body: Our hosting and messaging providers may store data on servers outside India. We use only providers that protect it to the standard Indian law requires.
privacy.sections.7.heading: How long we keep it
privacy.sections.7.body: If your enquiry does not go ahead, we delete your details and reports 24 months after your last contact with us. If you are treated, we keep your records for as long as the law requires, and then delete them.
privacy.sections.8.heading: Your rights
privacy.sections.8.body.0: You can ask us for a summary of the data we hold about you and who we have shared it with, ask us to correct or complete it, ask us to delete it, and withdraw your consent.
privacy.sections.8.body.1: You can name someone to use these rights for you if you die or cannot act yourself.
privacy.sections.8.body.2: To use any of these rights, write to us at the address below. We reply within 30 days.
privacy.sections.9.heading: Children
privacy.sections.9.body: If the patient is under 18, a parent or legal guardian must send the enquiry and give consent for them.
privacy.sections.10.heading: Complaints
privacy.sections.10.body: Write to us first at care@medsafar.com, with "Privacy" in the subject line. If you are not satisfied with our answer, you can complain to the Data Protection Board of India.
privacy.sections.11.heading: Changes to this policy
privacy.sections.11.body: If we change this policy, we put the new version on this page and change the date at the top. If a change affects how we use data you have already given us, we tell you first.

editorialPolicy.sections.0.body: We write for patients and families, many of whom read English as a second language. We use short sentences and common words, and we explain any medical term we cannot avoid.
editorialPolicy.sections.1.heading: Checked by a doctor
editorialPolicy.sections.1.body: Anything medical, such as what a treatment is, who needs it and how long recovery takes, is checked by a doctor before it is published. Until then it is marked as a draft on the page.
editorialPolicy.sections.2.heading: Sources

editorialPolicy.sections.5.heading: Keeping it up to date
editorialPolicy.sections.5.body: We review our pages regularly and when medical advice changes. Each policy page shows the date it was last updated.
editorialPolicy.sections.6.heading: Corrections

specialities.organ-transplant.name: Organ transplant
specialities.organ-transplant.summary: Kidney, liver and other organ transplants, often from a living family donor. The transplant team checks the patient and the donor, and the hospital's committee reviews the papers before anything is planned.
specialities.oncology.name: Oncology
specialities.oncology.summary: Cancer care: surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy and newer treatments. A team of cancer doctors reads the reports and plans treatment together.
specialities.haematology-bmt.name: Haematology and bone marrow transplant
specialities.haematology-bmt.summary: Care for blood disorders and blood cancers, including bone marrow transplants for adults and children.
specialities.neurology-neurosurgery.name: Neurology and neurosurgery
specialities.neurology-neurosurgery.summ: Care and surgery for the brain, spine and nerves, from tumours to movement disorders.
specialities.bariatric-surgery.name: Weight loss (bariatric) surgery
specialities.bariatric-surgery.summary: Operations that help people with severe obesity lose weight and keep it off, when diet and exercise have not been enough.
specialities.fertility-ivf.name: Fertility and IVF
specialities.fertility-ivf.summary: Help for couples who are trying to have a baby, including IVF and ICSI, after tests for both partners.
specialities.orthopaedics.name: Orthopaedics
specialities.orthopaedics.summary: Surgery for bones and joints, such as hip and knee replacement and the repair of sports injuries.
specialities.cardiology.name: Cardiology and heart surgery
specialities.cardiology.summary: Tests, procedures and operations for the heart, from angioplasty to bypass surgery and valve replacement.
specialities.cosmetic-plastic-surgery.su: Surgery to rebuild or reshape the body and face, and hair transplants, planned after a consultation with the surgeon.
specialities.ophthalmology.name: Eye care (ophthalmology)
specialities.ophthalmology.summary: Surgery and care for the eyes, from cataract and LASIK to cornea, glaucoma and retina treatment, after a full eye check.
specialities.dentistry.name: Dental care
specialities.dentistry.summary: Implants, root canal treatment, braces and cosmetic dentistry, planned after a check-up and X-rays.
treatments.kidney-transplant.name: Kidney transplant
treatments.kidney-transplant.summary: An operation that places a healthy kidney from a donor into a person whose own kidneys have stopped working.
treatments.kidney-transplant.what: A healthy kidney from a donor is placed in the lower belly and joined to the blood vessels and the bladder. The person's own kidneys are usually left where they are. The donor is most often a living family member; where the blood groups do not match, a swap (paired) transplant with another family can sometimes make it possible. Afterwards the patient takes medicines every day so the body does not reject the new kidney.
treatments.kidney-transplant.who: People whose kidneys have failed (end-stage kidney disease), whether or not they have started dialysis, who are fit enough for an operation and have a suitable donor.
treatments.kidney-transplant.stay: About 8 days: 3 in intensive care and 5 on the ward at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.kidney-transplant.recovery: Most people return to light daily life in 4 to 6 weeks. Plan to stay in India for about 4 to 6 weeks after the operation for close checks and blood tests.
treatments.kidney-transplant.faq.0.quest: Can a family member from my country be the donor?
treatments.kidney-transplant.faq.0.answe: Yes. Indian law allows living donation by close relatives, and the hospital's authorisation committee reviews every donor's documents before the transplant. We help you prepare these papers before you travel.
treatments.kidney-transplant.faq.1.quest: What if my donor's blood group does not match?
treatments.kidney-transplant.faq.1.answe: A swap (paired) transplant with another family, or a transplant across blood groups with extra treatment beforehand, may be possible. The transplant team decides after testing.
treatments.dialysis.name: Dialysis (haemodialysis and haemodiafiltration)
treatments.dialysis.summary: A machine cleans the blood when the kidneys can no longer do it, usually in sessions of about four hours, three times a week.
treatments.dialysis.what: Blood is passed through a filter outside the body that removes waste and extra fluid, then returned. Haemodiafiltration is a more thorough form of the same treatment. Sessions can also be done overnight (nocturnal dialysis) for some patients.
treatments.dialysis.who: People whose kidneys have failed, including those waiting for a transplant, and patients already on dialysis who need it while they are in India for treatment.
treatments.dialysis.stay: Usually done as a day patient: you come in for each session and go home the same day.
treatments.dialysis.recovery: Most people feel tired for a few hours after a session. Dialysis continues for as long as the kidneys do not work, or until a transplant.
treatments.dialysis.faq.0.question: I am already on dialysis. Can I continue it in India?
treatments.dialysis.faq.0.answer: Yes. Send us your current dialysis details and we book your sessions at the hospital for the whole of your stay.
treatments.dialysis.faq.1.question: Does dialysis replace a transplant?
treatments.dialysis.faq.1.answer: No. Dialysis does part of the kidneys' work. A transplant, where suitable, usually gives a better quality of life. The nephrologist advises which suits you.
treatments.liver-transplant.name: Liver transplant
treatments.liver-transplant.summary: An operation that replaces a failing liver with all or part of a healthy liver from a donor.
treatments.liver-transplant.what: The diseased liver is removed and replaced with a healthy one. In a living donor transplant, a family member gives part of their liver; both parts grow back to near full size within weeks. In a deceased donor transplant, a whole liver is used.
treatments.liver-transplant.who: People with liver failure from cirrhosis, hepatitis, alcohol or fatty liver disease, some liver cancers, or some rare inherited conditions, in adults and in children.
treatments.liver-transplant.stay: About 21 days at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.liver-transplant.recovery: Plan to stay in India for about 2 to 3 months in total. Most people return to normal daily life within 3 to 6 months, and take anti-rejection medicines for life.
treatments.liver-transplant.faq.0.questi: How long does the living donor stay in hospital?
treatments.liver-transplant.faq.0.answer: Usually about 7 to 10 days, and most donors return to normal life within 6 to 8 weeks.
treatments.liver-transplant.faq.1.questi: What tests are needed before we travel?
treatments.liver-transplant.faq.1.answer: Send us recent reports, scans and blood tests for the patient, and the blood group of possible donors. The transplant team tells you what else is needed.
treatments.pancreas-transplant.name: Pancreas transplant
treatments.pancreas-transplant.summary: An operation that places a healthy pancreas from a donor into a person with diabetes, so their body makes its own insulin again. It is often done together with a kidney transplant.
treatments.pancreas-transplant.what: A pancreas from a deceased donor is placed in the lower belly and joined to the blood vessels and the bowel or bladder. The person's own pancreas stays in place. When the new pancreas works, insulin injections are no longer needed. It is often done at the same time as a kidney transplant.
treatments.pancreas-transplant.who: Mainly people with type 1 diabetes: those who no longer feel the warning signs of a dangerously low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia unawareness), those who develop kidney, nerve or eye damage despite insulin, and those who also have chronic kidney disease. Some people with type 2 diabetes are also suitable. Diabetes with kidney disease is serious: the risk of death is about twice that of kidney disease alone, average survival is about 4 to 5 years, and around 16 years of life are lost.
treatments.pancreas-transplant.stay: Usually about 2 to 3 weeks in hospital, longer when done with a kidney transplant. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.pancreas-transplant.recovery: Plan to stay in India for about 2 to 3 months. Anti-rejection medicines are taken for life.
treatments.pancreas-transplant.faq.0.ans: Yes. The pancreas comes from a deceased donor, so there is a waiting list. The team explains how it works for international patients.
treatments.pancreas-transplant.faq.1.ans: If the new pancreas works well, no. Your doctors check your blood sugar closely in the first weeks.
treatments.intestine-transplant.name: Intestine transplant
treatments.intestine-transplant.summary: An operation that replaces a small intestine that has failed or been lost with a healthy intestine from a donor.
treatments.intestine-transplant.what: A small intestine from a donor is joined to the patient's blood vessels and bowel, so they can absorb food again and stop drip feeding. It is one of the most complex transplants and needs long, close follow-up.
treatments.intestine-transplant.who: In children, intestinal failure after necrotising enterocolitis (NEC), gastroschisis or a motility disorder. In adults, loss of the intestine from mesenteric ischaemia (a blocked blood supply), midgut volvulus (a twisted gut) or tumours of the mesentery.
treatments.intestine-transplant.stay: Usually 4 to 8 weeks in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.intestine-transplant.recovery: Plan to stay in India for about 3 months or more. Eating is brought back slowly, and anti-rejection medicines are taken for life.
treatments.intestine-transplant.faq.0.qu: Who is it for if I am fed through a drip at home?
treatments.intestine-transplant.faq.0.an: People who depend on drip feeding (parenteral nutrition) and develop problems with it, such as liver damage or repeated line infections, are usually assessed for a transplant.
treatments.intestine-transplant.faq.1.an: Yes. Many intestine transplants are done in children. The team assesses each child separately.
treatments.hand-transplant.name: Hand transplant
treatments.hand-transplant.summary: An operation that attaches one or both hands from a deceased donor to a person who has lost theirs, joining bone, blood vessels, tendons, nerves and skin.
treatments.hand-transplant.what: A hand transplant moves skin, muscle, tendon, bone, blood vessels and nerves together, which is why it is called a composite tissue transplant. Surgeons fix the bones, join the arteries and veins, repair the tendons and connect the nerves. Afterwards the patient takes medicine to stop the body rejecting the new hands, and has long-term physiotherapy. When it succeeds, a hand transplant can bring back feeling, a sense of position and coordinated movement beyond what a prosthetic hand can give.
treatments.hand-transplant.who: People who have lost one or both hands or arms, after careful medical, psychological and immune testing. A suitable donor has to be found, so there is usually a waiting period.
treatments.hand-transplant.stay: Usually about 3 to 4 weeks in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.hand-transplant.recovery: Plan to stay in India for about 3 to 6 months for daily hand therapy. Movement and feeling keep improving for one to two years as the nerves grow.
treatments.hand-transplant.faq.0.questio: How soon can I use the new hand?
treatments.hand-transplant.faq.0.answer: Simple movements usually start within weeks. Feeling and finer control come back slowly over months, with daily therapy.
treatments.hand-transplant.faq.1.questio: Will I need medicines for life?
treatments.hand-transplant.faq.1.answer: Yes. Like any transplant, it needs anti-rejection medicines every day, and regular checks.
treatments.bone-marrow-transplant.name: Bone marrow transplant (stem cell transplant)
treatments.bone-marrow-transplant.summar: A treatment that replaces damaged or diseased bone marrow with healthy blood-forming stem cells, used for some blood cancers and blood disorders.
treatments.bone-marrow-transplant.what: First, strong chemotherapy, sometimes with radiation, clears the diseased marrow. Then healthy stem cells are given through a drip, much like a blood transfusion, and settle in the bones to make new blood. The cells come from the patient (autologous), from a matched donor (allogeneic), or from a half-matched family member (haploidentical), which means most patients can find a donor.
treatments.bone-marrow-transplant.who: People with some blood cancers, such as leukaemia, lymphoma and myeloma, and some blood disorders, such as thalassaemia, sickle cell disease and aplastic anaemia, in adults and in children.
treatments.bone-marrow-transplant.stay: About 30 days at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.bone-marrow-transplant.recove: Plan to stay in India for about 2 to 3 months after the transplant for close follow-up. The immune system takes 6 to 12 months to recover fully.
A brother or sister is checked first. If none is a full match, a half-matched parent, child or sibling can often donate. Testing is done before you travel or soon after you arrive.
Usually not. Most stem cells today are collected from the donor's blood through a drip, over a few hours.
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.name: CAR-T cell therapy
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.summary: The patient's own immune cells are collected, changed in a laboratory to recognise their cancer, and given back by drip. Used for some leukaemias, lymphomas and myeloma.
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.what: White blood cells called T cells are collected from the patient's blood. In a laboratory they are given a new receptor (CAR) that helps them find and attack the cancer. After a short course of chemotherapy, the cells are given back through a drip, where they multiply and fight the cancer.
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.who: Adults and some children with certain leukaemias, lymphomas or multiple myeloma that have come back or not responded to other treatment.
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.stay: Usually about 2 weeks in hospital after the cells are given. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.recovery: Plan to stay near the hospital for about 4 weeks after the infusion, as side effects such as fever can appear in this time. Most people go home within 1 to 2 months.
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.faq.0.ques: How long does it take to make the cells?
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.faq.0.answ: Usually a few weeks from collection to infusion. Your doctor may give other treatment while you wait.
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.faq.1.ques: What are the main side effects?
treatments.car-t-cell-therapy.faq.1.answ: Fever, low blood pressure and, sometimes, confusion in the first weeks. The team watches closely and treats them early.
treatments.childhood-cancer-treatment.na: Treatment for children's cancers and blood disorders
treatments.childhood-cancer-treatment.su: Care for children with leukaemia, lymphoma, solid tumours and non-cancerous blood disorders, planned by doctors who treat only children.
treatments.childhood-cancer-treatment.wh: A paediatric haemato-oncologist plans the whole treatment, which may combine chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy and bone marrow transplant. Doses and care are suited to a growing child, with support for the family throughout.
Children with blood cancers such as leukaemia and lymphoma, solid tumours, or blood disorders such as thalassaemia and aplastic anaemia.
treatments.childhood-cancer-treatment.st: Depends on the treatment plan. Many chemotherapy sessions are day care; a bone marrow transplant needs about a month in hospital.
treatments.childhood-cancer-treatment.re: Treatment often lasts several months. The doctor explains which parts must be done in India and which can continue at home.
treatments.childhood-cancer-treatment.fa: Can one parent stay with the child?
Yes. A parent can stay with the child in hospital. We help with nearby accommodation for the rest of the family.
Can part of the treatment continue at home?
Often, yes. The doctor can share the plan with your local doctor for the parts that can safely be done at home.
treatments.chemotherapy.name: Chemotherapy
treatments.chemotherapy.summary: Medicines that kill cancer cells or stop them growing, given by drip, injection or tablet over a series of sessions.
treatments.chemotherapy.what: A medical oncologist chooses the medicines, dose and timing for the type and stage of cancer. Treatment is usually given in cycles, with rest weeks in between so the body can recover. It can be given before surgery to shrink a tumour, after surgery to lower the chance of it coming back, or on its own.
treatments.chemotherapy.who: People with many kinds of cancer, including breast, lung, bowel, ovarian, head and neck, blood and bone cancers. Your oncologist decides whether it suits your case.
treatments.chemotherapy.stay: Most sessions are day care: you come in, have the drip and go home the same day.
treatments.chemotherapy.recovery: Tiredness and other side effects usually ease within days to weeks of each cycle. A full course often takes 3 to 6 months.
treatments.chemotherapy.faq.0.question: Do I need to stay in India for the whole course?
treatments.chemotherapy.faq.0.answer: Not always. Often the first cycles are given in India and the rest can continue at home, with the plan shared with your local oncologist.
treatments.chemotherapy.faq.1.question: Will I lose my hair?
treatments.chemotherapy.faq.1.answer: With some medicines, yes, and it usually grows back after treatment. Many modern medicines do not cause hair loss.
treatments.targeted-therapy-immunotherap: Newer cancer medicines that attack a specific weakness in the cancer, or help the body's own immune system fight it.

Tests on the tumour look for changes in its genes or proteins. Targeted medicines block those changes, so they act mainly on cancer cells. Immunotherapy helps the immune system recognise and attack the cancer. These are often called precision or molecular oncology, and are given by drip or as tablets.
People whose cancer shows a matching change on testing, or whose cancer type is known to respond, such as some lung, breast, kidney, bowel, skin and head and neck cancers.
Usually day care, or tablets taken at home.
Most people continue their normal daily life during treatment, with regular checks and scans.
How do I know if it suits me?
Your oncologist looks at your tumour test results. If testing has not been done, it can often be done on the biopsy you already have.
Is it the same as chemotherapy?
No. It works in a different way and usually has different, often milder, side effects. Sometimes it is given together with chemotherapy.
treatments.radiation-therapy.name: Radiation therapy (radiotherapy)
treatments.radiation-therapy.summary: Treatment that uses carefully aimed high-energy beams to destroy cancer cells in one part of the body.
treatments.radiation-therapy.what: A planning scan maps the tumour, and a machine then aims beams at it from several angles, sparing the healthy tissue around it as much as possible. Each session takes minutes and is painless. Treatment is usually given on weekdays for one to several weeks.
treatments.radiation-therapy.who: People with many kinds of cancer, on its own or with surgery and chemotherapy, and sometimes to ease pain from cancer that has spread.
treatments.radiation-therapy.stay: Usually no hospital stay: you come in for each short session.
treatments.radiation-therapy.recovery: Tiredness and skin soreness in the treated area are common and usually settle within a few weeks after the course.
treatments.radiation-therapy.faq.0.answe: No. With external beam radiotherapy you are not radioactive, and it is safe to be with family.
treatments.radiation-therapy.faq.1.quest: How long will I need to stay in India?
treatments.radiation-therapy.faq.1.answe: As long as the course lasts, usually 1 to 7 weeks, plus a few days for planning. Your doctor tells you the exact length.
treatments.cancer-surgery.name: Cancer surgery (surgical oncology)
treatments.cancer-surgery.summary: An operation to remove a tumour and, where needed, nearby tissue or lymph nodes.
treatments.cancer-surgery.what: A surgical oncologist removes the tumour with a margin of healthy tissue, and often the nearby lymph nodes to check for spread. Where it suits the case, it is done by keyhole (laparoscopic) or robotic surgery, which usually means smaller cuts and a quicker recovery. The removed tissue is examined to plan any further treatment.
treatments.cancer-surgery.who: People with solid tumours, such as head and neck, breast, stomach, bowel, liver, pancreas, kidney, bladder, prostate, womb, ovary, bone and soft tissue cancers.
treatments.cancer-surgery.stay: Usually 2 to 10 days in hospital, depending on the operation. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.cancer-surgery.recovery: From 2 weeks for smaller operations to 6 to 8 weeks for major ones. Plan to stay in India until the stitches are checked and the report is discussed.
treatments.cancer-surgery.faq.0.question: Will I need other treatment after surgery?
treatments.cancer-surgery.faq.0.answer: Sometimes. The report on the removed tissue shows whether chemotherapy or radiotherapy would help. The team discusses this with you before you go home.
treatments.cancer-surgery.faq.1.question: Can it be done by robotic surgery?
treatments.cancer-surgery.faq.1.answer: For many cancers, yes. The surgeon decides based on the tumour and your scans.
treatments.head-neck-cancer-surgery.name: Head and neck cancer surgery
treatments.head-neck-cancer-surgery.summ: Surgery for cancers of the mouth, tongue, throat, voice box, salivary glands and sinuses, saving speech and swallowing wherever possible.
treatments.head-neck-cancer-surgery.what: The tumour is removed, often with the lymph nodes in the neck. Where it suits the case, it is done through the mouth with a laser or a robot (transoral surgery), avoiding large cuts. When the voice box is involved, voice-preserving surgery is chosen where possible, and voice rehabilitation is offered when it is not. Reconstruction can rebuild the area in the same operation.
treatments.head-neck-cancer-surgery.who: People with cancer of the mouth, tongue, cheek, throat, voice box (larynx), salivary glands, nose or sinuses.
treatments.head-neck-cancer-surgery.stay: Usually 3 to 10 days in hospital, longer if reconstruction is needed. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.head-neck-cancer-surgery.reco: Usually 3 to 6 weeks. Speech and swallowing therapy may be needed. Radiotherapy is sometimes given afterwards.
Will I be able to speak and eat normally?
The surgeon aims to keep speech and swallowing wherever possible, and therapists help you recover them after surgery.
Surgery done through the open mouth using robotic arms or a laser, so there is no cut on the face or neck for the tumour itself.
treatments.thyroid-surgery.name: Thyroid and parathyroid surgery
treatments.thyroid-surgery.summary: An operation to remove part or all of the thyroid or a parathyroid gland in the neck, for cancer, large lumps or overactive glands.
treatments.thyroid-surgery.what: Through a small cut in the front of the neck, the surgeon removes half or all of the thyroid gland, or an overactive parathyroid gland, taking care to protect the nerves to the voice box. If the whole thyroid is removed, a daily tablet replaces its hormone.
treatments.thyroid-surgery.who: People with thyroid cancer, thyroid lumps that are large or suspicious, an overactive thyroid that does not settle with medicine, or an overactive parathyroid gland.
treatments.thyroid-surgery.stay: Usually 1 to 3 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.thyroid-surgery.recovery: Most people return to normal activity in 1 to 2 weeks.
treatments.thyroid-surgery.faq.0.answer: Rarely. The surgeon protects the voice nerves, and any hoarseness after surgery usually settles within weeks.
treatments.thyroid-surgery.faq.1.answer: If all the thyroid is removed, yes, a daily thyroid hormone tablet for life. If half is removed, often not.
treatments.breast-cancer-surgery.name: Breast cancer surgery
treatments.breast-cancer-surgery.summary: An operation to remove breast cancer, with the breast kept or rebuilt wherever possible.
treatments.breast-cancer-surgery.what: Where it is safe, only the tumour and a margin around it are removed (breast-conserving surgery), and the breast is reshaped in the same operation (oncoplastic surgery). Where the whole breast must be removed (mastectomy), it can often be rebuilt. The lymph nodes in the armpit are checked, usually with a small sampling operation. A vacuum-assisted biopsy can be used to diagnose or remove small lumps without open surgery.
treatments.breast-cancer-surgery.who: Women, and occasionally men, with breast cancer, and people with a strong family history who may benefit from genetic testing.
treatments.breast-cancer-surgery.stay: Usually 1 to 3 days in hospital, longer with reconstruction. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.breast-cancer-surgery.recover: Usually 2 to 4 weeks. Chemotherapy, radiotherapy or hormone tablets may follow, depending on the report.
treatments.breast-cancer-surgery.faq.0.a: Often, yes, especially when the tumour is small compared with the breast, or after chemotherapy shrinks it. The surgeon advises after reviewing your scans.
treatments.breast-cancer-surgery.faq.1.a: If you were diagnosed young or have close relatives with breast or ovarian cancer, testing may help plan your treatment. The doctor advises.
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.name: Liver, pancreas and bile duct cancer surgery (including Whipple)
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.summary: Surgery to remove cancers of the liver, pancreas, bile duct and gall bladder, including the Whipple operation for the pancreas.
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.what: Part of the liver can be removed safely, and what remains grows back. For cancer at the head of the pancreas, the Whipple operation (pancreaticoduodenectomy) removes it with part of the bowel and bile duct, then reconnects them. Where tumours involve major blood vessels, these can be removed and rebuilt in the same operation. Many of these operations can be done by keyhole or robotic surgery.
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.who: People with cancers of the liver, bile duct, gall bladder or pancreas, and cancers that have spread to the liver from the bowel, after scans show the tumour can be removed.
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.stay: Usually 7 to 14 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.recovery: Usually 6 to 8 weeks. Plan to stay in India for about 3 to 4 weeks after surgery.
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.faq.0.ques: Can I live a normal life after part of my liver is removed?
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.faq.0.answ: Yes. The liver grows back to near full size within weeks, as long as the remaining part is healthy.
treatments.hpb-cancer-surgery.faq.1.answ: An operation that removes the head of the pancreas, part of the small bowel, the gall bladder and part of the bile duct, then reconnects them. It is the main operation for cancer in that area.
treatments.gi-cancer-surgery.name: Stomach, bowel and food pipe cancer surgery
treatments.gi-cancer-surgery.summary: Surgery to remove cancers of the food pipe (oesophagus), stomach, small bowel, colon and rectum.
treatments.gi-cancer-surgery.what: The part of the gut with the cancer is removed with its lymph nodes, and the ends are joined again. Most of these operations can be done by keyhole or robotic surgery. For rectal cancer, the surgeon aims to keep normal bowel control wherever possible.
treatments.gi-cancer-surgery.who: People with cancer of the oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, colon or rectum, and some abdominal tumours such as sarcomas.
treatments.gi-cancer-surgery.stay: Usually 5 to 10 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.gi-cancer-surgery.recovery: Usually 4 to 8 weeks. Eating returns slowly, with advice from a dietitian.
treatments.gi-cancer-surgery.faq.0.answe: Not always. Sometimes a temporary stoma protects the join while it heals, and is closed a few months later. The surgeon tells you before the operation.
treatments.gi-cancer-surgery.faq.1.answe: Often, before or after surgery, depending on the stage. The team plans it together.
treatments.hipec.name: Cytoreductive surgery and HIPEC
treatments.hipec.summary: Surgery that removes all visible cancer from inside the belly, followed by heated chemotherapy washed through the belly during the same operation.
treatments.hipec.what: The surgeon removes every visible tumour from the lining of the belly (cytoreductive surgery). Then, while still in theatre, heated chemotherapy is circulated through the belly for about an hour (HIPEC) to treat cancer cells too small to see. Heat helps the medicine work better, and little of it reaches the rest of the body.
treatments.hipec.who: Selected people with cancer that has spread to the lining of the belly (peritoneum) from the ovary, bowel, appendix or stomach, and people with peritoneal mesothelioma or pseudomyxoma.
treatments.hipec.stay: Usually 10 to 14 days in hospital, with a few days in intensive care. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.hipec.recovery: Usually 6 to 12 weeks. Plan to stay in India for about 4 weeks after surgery.
treatments.hipec.faq.0.question: Is everyone with spread to the belly suitable?
treatments.hipec.faq.0.answer: No. The team reviews your scans and health to see whether all the visible cancer can be removed, which is when HIPEC helps most.
treatments.hipec.faq.1.question: Is it a long operation?
treatments.hipec.faq.1.answer: Yes, often 8 to 12 hours. It is done only in specialised centres with experienced teams.
treatments.urologic-cancer-surgery.name: Kidney, bladder and prostate cancer surgery
treatments.urologic-cancer-surgery.summa: Surgery for cancers of the kidney, bladder, prostate, testis and adrenal gland, often done robotically.
treatments.urologic-cancer-surgery.what: Depending on the cancer, the surgeon removes the tumour with part of the kidney (keeping the rest working) or the whole kidney, the prostate, or the bladder. When the bladder is removed, a new way to pass urine is made, sometimes a new bladder from bowel. Robotic surgery is used where it suits, and the surgeon aims to keep bladder control and sexual function wherever possible.
treatments.urologic-cancer-surgery.who: People with cancer of the kidney, bladder, prostate, testis, penis or adrenal gland.
treatments.urologic-cancer-surgery.stay: Usually 3 to 10 days in hospital, depending on the operation. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.urologic-cancer-surgery.faq.0: Can part of my kidney be kept?
Often, for small tumours. Removing only the tumour (partial nephrectomy) keeps more kidney function.
treatments.urologic-cancer-surgery.faq.1: Will prostate surgery affect bladder control?
Some leakage is common at first and usually improves over weeks to months, with exercises. The surgeon explains your own risk.
treatments.gynaecologic-cancer-surgery.n: Ovarian, womb and cervical cancer surgery
treatments.gynaecologic-cancer-surgery.s: Surgery for cancers of the ovary, womb (uterus), cervix and vulva, keeping fertility where it is safe.
treatments.gynaecologic-cancer-surgery.w: The surgeon removes the cancer and, where needed, the womb, ovaries and nearby lymph nodes. For advanced ovarian cancer, extensive (ultra-radical) surgery aims to remove all visible disease. In young women with early cancer, fertility-sparing surgery may keep the womb or an ovary. Keyhole and robotic surgery are used where they suit.
Women with cancer of the ovary, womb, cervix or vulva, and some gynaecological sarcomas.
treatments.gynaecologic-cancer-surgery.s: Usually 3 to 10 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.gynaecologic-cancer-surgery.r: Usually 4 to 6 weeks. Chemotherapy or radiotherapy may follow.
treatments.gynaecologic-cancer-surgery.f: Sometimes, for early cancers in young women. Tell the doctor if this matters to you, so it is part of the plan from the start.
For some advanced ovarian cancers, yes, to shrink the disease first. The team decides from your scans.
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.name: Bone cancer surgery (limb salvage)
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.summary: Surgery that removes a bone or soft tissue tumour while saving the arm or leg, instead of amputating it.
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.what: The tumour is removed with a margin of healthy tissue, and the missing bone is rebuilt with a metal implant (endoprosthesis), bone from a bone bank, or the patient's own bone. Most people with bone cancer today keep their limb. Chemotherapy is often given before and after surgery.
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.who: Children and adults with bone cancers such as osteosarcoma and Ewing's sarcoma, soft tissue sarcomas, some non-cancerous but aggressive bone tumours, and cancer that has spread to bone.
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.stay: Usually 5 to 10 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.recovery: Usually 6 to 12 weeks, with physiotherapy to walk or use the arm again.
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.faq.0.ans: In most cases, no. Limb salvage is possible for most bone tumours. The surgeon tells you after reviewing your scans.
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.faq.1.que: How long does the implant last?
treatments.bone-cancer-surgery.faq.1.ans: Many last many years. Some may need replacing later, especially in children who are still growing.
treatments.liver-tumour-embolisation.sum: Through a pinhole in the groin or wrist, a fine tube is guided to the artery feeding a liver tumour, and chemotherapy (TACE) or tiny radioactive beads (TARE) are delivered straight into it.
treatments.liver-tumour-embolisation.wha: An interventional radiologist guides a fine tube through an artery to the liver using X-ray imaging. In TACE (chemoembolisation), chemotherapy is delivered into the tumour and its blood supply is blocked. In TARE (radioembolisation), tiny beads carrying radiation are delivered instead. There is no open surgery, only a pinhole.
treatments.liver-tumour-embolisation.who: People with liver cancer, or cancer that has spread to the liver, that cannot be removed by surgery, or as a bridge to surgery or a transplant.
treatments.liver-tumour-embolisation.sta: Usually 1 to 2 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.liver-tumour-embolisation.rec: Most people feel tired, with some pain or fever, for about a week, then return to normal life.
treatments.liver-tumour-embolisation.faq: It is done under local anaesthetic and sedation. Some pain and fever afterwards is common and is treated with medicines.
Will I need more than one session?
Sometimes. A scan after about 4 to 6 weeks shows how the tumour has responded.
treatments.tumour-ablation.name: Tumour ablation (radiofrequency and microwave)
treatments.tumour-ablation.summary: A needle guided by a scan destroys a small tumour with heat, without open surgery.
treatments.tumour-ablation.what: Using ultrasound or CT, an interventional radiologist places a thin needle into the tumour through the skin. The needle heats the tumour with radio waves or microwaves until it is destroyed. It takes about an hour, leaves only a pinhole, and can be repeated.
treatments.tumour-ablation.who: People with small tumours in the liver, kidney, lung or bone, especially those not suited to surgery.
treatments.tumour-ablation.stay: Usually 1 day in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.tumour-ablation.recovery: Most people return to normal activity within a few days.
treatments.tumour-ablation.faq.0.questio: Is it as good as surgery?
treatments.tumour-ablation.faq.0.answer: For some small tumours the results are close to surgery. The team advises which suits your tumour.
treatments.tumour-ablation.faq.1.questio: How will I know it worked?
treatments.tumour-ablation.faq.1.answer: A scan, usually about a month later, checks that the whole tumour has been treated.
treatments.brain-tumour-surgery.name: Brain tumour surgery (craniotomy)
treatments.brain-tumour-surgery.summary: An operation in which the surgeon opens a small part of the skull to remove or reduce a tumour in the brain.
treatments.brain-tumour-surgery.what: A small window of skull is lifted, the tumour is removed as fully as is safe, and the bone is put back. Navigation and a surgical microscope guide the surgeon, and some operations are done with the patient awake to protect speech and movement. The tissue is examined to plan further treatment.
treatments.brain-tumour-surgery.who: People with brain tumours, whether cancerous or not, such as gliomas, meningiomas, pituitary tumours and tumours that have spread to the brain.
treatments.brain-tumour-surgery.stay: About 5 days: 1 in intensive care and 4 on the ward at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.brain-tumour-surgery.recovery: Usually 4 to 8 weeks. Plan to stay in India for about 2 weeks after surgery.
treatments.brain-tumour-surgery.faq.0.an: Usually only a small strip, and hair grows back over the scar.
treatments.brain-tumour-surgery.faq.1.an: It depends on the type of tumour. The report on the removed tissue guides this.
treatments.deep-brain-stimulation.name: Deep brain stimulation (DBS)
treatments.deep-brain-stimulation.summar: A small device placed under the skin sends mild electrical signals to part of the brain, used for some movement disorders such as Parkinson's disease.
treatments.deep-brain-stimulation.what: Thin wires are placed in a precise spot deep in the brain and connected to a small battery under the skin of the chest, like a pacemaker. The signals calm the faulty brain activity that causes shaking and stiffness. Settings are adjusted over the following weeks.
treatments.deep-brain-stimulation.who: People with Parkinson's disease whose medicines no longer control their symptoms well, and some people with tremor or dystonia.
treatments.deep-brain-stimulation.stay: Usually 3 to 5 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.deep-brain-stimulation.recove: Usually 2 to 4 weeks, with settings tuned over a few visits.
No, but it can greatly reduce shaking, stiffness and the swings of medicine, and often lets people take less medicine.
Can the settings be changed after I go home?
Yes. Settings can be adjusted at later visits, and many devices can be checked by a neurologist at home.
treatments.spinal-fusion.name: Spinal fusion
treatments.spinal-fusion.summary: An operation that joins two or more bones of the spine so they heal into one, to steady a painful or unstable part of the back or neck.
treatments.spinal-fusion.what: Screws and rods hold the bones still while bone graft helps them grow together. Where it suits the case, it is done by minimally invasive surgery through small cuts, with navigation to place the screws precisely, which usually means less pain and a quicker return home.
treatments.spinal-fusion.who: People with an unstable or slipped spine (spondylolisthesis), severe disc wear, fractures, deformity, or tumours of the spine, when other treatment has not helped.
treatments.spinal-fusion.stay: About 5 days for up to two levels: 1 in intensive care and 4 on the ward at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.spinal-fusion.recovery: Walking starts the day after surgery. Most people return to light work in 4 to 6 weeks, and the bones fuse over 3 to 6 months.
treatments.spinal-fusion.faq.0.question: Will I lose movement in my back?
treatments.spinal-fusion.faq.0.answer: Fusing one or two levels makes little difference to everyday movement.
treatments.spinal-fusion.faq.1.question: When can I fly home?
treatments.spinal-fusion.faq.1.answer: Usually about 2 weeks after surgery, once the wound is checked.
treatments.acdf.name: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF)
treatments.acdf.summary: Through a small cut at the front of the neck, a damaged disc pressing on the nerves or spinal cord is removed and the bones either side are joined.
treatments.acdf.what: The surgeon reaches the spine from the front of the neck, removes the worn or slipped disc and any bone spurs pressing on the nerves, and places a small spacer so the two bones grow together.
treatments.acdf.who: People with arm pain, numbness or weakness, or problems with balance and hand use, from a slipped or worn disc in the neck.
treatments.acdf.stay: About 4 days: 1 in intensive care and 3 on the ward at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.acdf.recovery: Most people return to light activity in 2 to 4 weeks.
treatments.acdf.faq.0.question: Is a disc replacement better?
treatments.acdf.faq.0.answer: For some people, a disc replacement keeps movement in the neck instead of joining the bones. The surgeon advises which suits you.
treatments.acdf.faq.1.question: Will I have trouble swallowing?
treatments.acdf.faq.1.answer: A mild sore throat or difficulty swallowing for a few days is common and usually settles quickly.
treatments.cervical-disc-replacement.sum: A worn or slipped disc in the neck is replaced with an artificial disc that keeps the neck moving.
treatments.cervical-disc-replacement.wha: Through a small cut at the front of the neck, the damaged disc is removed and an artificial disc is put in its place. Unlike fusion, the joint keeps moving, which may protect the discs above and below.
treatments.cervical-disc-replacement.who: Younger, active people with arm pain or numbness from one or two worn or slipped discs in the neck, without major arthritis in the joints.
treatments.cervical-disc-replacement.sta: Usually 2 to 3 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.cervical-disc-replacement.rec: Most people return to light activity in 2 to 3 weeks.
treatments.cervical-disc-replacement.faq: People with severe arthritis of the neck joints, an unstable spine or weak bones are usually better suited to fusion.
How long does the artificial disc last?
Modern artificial discs are designed to last many years. The surgeon explains the type used.
treatments.microdiscectomy.name: Microdiscectomy and laminectomy
treatments.microdiscectomy.summary: Keyhole surgery on the lower back that removes the part of a slipped disc, or of the bone, that is pressing on a nerve, to relieve sciatica and leg pain.
treatments.microdiscectomy.what: Through a small cut, using a microscope, the surgeon removes the piece of disc pressing on the nerve (microdiscectomy) or widens a narrowed spinal canal by removing a little bone (laminectomy).
treatments.microdiscectomy.who: People with sciatica or leg pain, numbness or weakness from a slipped disc or a narrowed spinal canal, when medicines and physiotherapy have not helped.
treatments.microdiscectomy.stay: About 3 days on the ward at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.microdiscectomy.recovery: Leg pain often eases straight away. Most people return to light work in 2 to 4 weeks.
treatments.microdiscectomy.faq.0.answer: Sometimes. Physiotherapy and core exercises help lower the chance.
treatments.microdiscectomy.faq.1.answer: Often, yes. Endoscopic surgery uses an even smaller cut. The surgeon advises which suits your disc.
treatments.endoscopic-spine-surgery.name: Endoscopic spine surgery
treatments.endoscopic-spine-surgery.summ: Spine surgery through a cut of about one centimetre, using a thin camera, to free a trapped nerve.
treatments.endoscopic-spine-surgery.what: A thin tube with a camera (endoscope) is passed to the spine through a very small cut. The surgeon removes the slipped disc or bone pressing on the nerve while watching on a screen. Muscles are moved aside rather than cut.
treatments.endoscopic-spine-surgery.who: People with sciatica or arm pain from a slipped disc, or a narrowed spinal canal at one or two levels.
treatments.endoscopic-spine-surgery.stay: Often the same day or 1 night in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.endoscopic-spine-surgery.reco: Most people walk within hours and return to light work in 1 to 2 weeks.
Is it done under general anaesthetic?
Sometimes under local anaesthetic with sedation, sometimes general. The team decides with you.
Is it suitable for every spine problem?
No. It suits trapped nerves at one or two levels. Instability or deformity usually needs fixation.
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.name: Spine deformity correction (scoliosis)
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.summary: Surgery that straightens and steadies a curved spine, in teenagers and adults.
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.what: Screws and rods are fixed to the spine to straighten the curve and hold it while the bones fuse. Navigation and nerve monitoring during surgery help keep it safe.
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.who: Teenagers and adults with a spine curve (scoliosis or kyphosis) that is large, getting worse, or causing pain or breathing problems.
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.stay: Usually 5 to 7 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.recovery: Walking starts within a day or two. School or desk work usually resumes in 4 to 6 weeks, and sport in 6 to 12 months.
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.faq.0.quest: Will my child grow normally after surgery?
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.faq.0.answe: Surgery is usually timed near the end of growth. The surgeon explains the best timing for your child.
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.faq.1.quest: How straight will the spine be?
treatments.scoliosis-surgery.faq.1.answe: Most curves are greatly reduced, though not always made fully straight. Balance and comfort are the main aims.
treatments.gastric-sleeve.name: Sleeve gastrectomy (gastric sleeve)
treatments.gastric-sleeve.summary: Keyhole surgery that removes a large part of the stomach, leaving a narrow sleeve, so a person feels full sooner.
treatments.gastric-sleeve.what: About three quarters of the stomach is removed by keyhole surgery, leaving a narrow tube. The smaller stomach holds less food and makes less of the hormone that causes hunger.
treatments.gastric-sleeve.who: Adults with a body mass index (BMI) of about 35 or more, or 30 or more with diabetes, high blood pressure or sleep apnoea, after diet and exercise have not worked. Thresholds can be lower for people of Asian origin.
treatments.gastric-sleeve.stay: Usually 2 to 3 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.gastric-sleeve.recovery: Most people return to desk work in 1 to 2 weeks, moving from liquids to normal food over about 6 weeks.
treatments.gastric-sleeve.faq.0.question: How much weight will I lose?
treatments.gastric-sleeve.faq.0.answer: Many people lose about 60 to 70 percent of their excess weight within one to two years, with diet and exercise.
treatments.gastric-sleeve.faq.1.question: Will I need vitamins afterwards?
treatments.gastric-sleeve.faq.1.answer: Yes, usually daily vitamins and regular blood tests.
treatments.gastric-bypass.name: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
treatments.gastric-bypass.summary: Surgery that makes a small stomach pouch and connects it further down the small intestine, so less food is eaten and absorbed.
treatments.gastric-bypass.what: By keyhole surgery, a small pouch is made at the top of the stomach and joined directly to a lower part of the small intestine, bypassing the rest of the stomach. Less food fits, and fewer calories are absorbed.
treatments.gastric-bypass.who: Adults with severe obesity, especially those with type 2 diabetes or bad acid reflux, after other methods have not worked.
treatments.gastric-bypass.stay: Usually 2 to 4 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.gastric-bypass.recovery: Most people return to desk work in 2 weeks, with a staged diet over about 6 weeks.
treatments.gastric-bypass.faq.0.question: Will it help my diabetes?
treatments.gastric-bypass.faq.0.answer: Often, yes. Many people need less diabetes medicine, and some stop it, after a bypass.
treatments.gastric-bypass.faq.1.question: Sleeve or bypass: which is right for me?
treatments.gastric-bypass.faq.1.answer: It depends on your weight, reflux, diabetes and other health. The surgeon advises after assessment.
treatments.ivf.name: In vitro fertilisation (IVF)
treatments.ivf.summary: Eggs are collected and fertilised with sperm in a laboratory, and an embryo is then placed in the womb.
treatments.ivf.what: Hormone injections help the ovaries produce several eggs, which are collected in a short procedure under sedation. They are mixed with sperm in the laboratory, and after a few days one embryo is placed in the womb through a thin tube. Spare embryos can be frozen.
treatments.ivf.who: Couples who have not conceived after trying, including with blocked tubes, low egg reserve, endometriosis, or unexplained infertility.
treatments.ivf.stay: No hospital stay: egg collection and embryo transfer are day procedures.
treatments.ivf.recovery: Most women return to normal activity the day after each procedure. One cycle takes about 3 to 4 weeks in India; a pregnancy test follows about 2 weeks after transfer.
treatments.ivf.faq.0.question: How long do we need to be in India?
treatments.ivf.faq.0.answer: Usually about 3 to 4 weeks for one cycle. Some early tests and injections can be started at home.
treatments.ivf.faq.1.question: What are the chances of success?
treatments.ivf.faq.1.answer: They depend mostly on the woman's age and the cause of infertility. The doctor gives you an estimate after tests.
treatments.icsi.name: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI)
treatments.icsi.summary: A form of IVF in which a single sperm is injected directly into each egg, often used when there are problems with sperm.
treatments.icsi.what: It follows the same steps as IVF, but instead of mixing eggs and sperm, an embryologist injects one sperm into each egg under a microscope. Sperm can also be collected directly from the testis when there is none in the semen.
treatments.icsi.who: Couples where the man has a low sperm count, poorly moving sperm or no sperm in the semen, or where IVF has not led to fertilisation before.
treatments.icsi.stay: No hospital stay: all steps are day procedures.
treatments.icsi.recovery: As for IVF: about 3 to 4 weeks in India for one cycle.
treatments.icsi.faq.0.question: What if there is no sperm in the semen?
treatments.icsi.faq.0.answer: Sperm can often be taken from the testis in a minor procedure and used for ICSI.
treatments.icsi.faq.1.question: Is ICSI more successful than IVF?
treatments.icsi.faq.1.answer: Not in general. It helps mainly when the problem is with the sperm.
treatments.knee-replacement.name: Total knee replacement
treatments.knee-replacement.summary: An operation that replaces the worn surfaces of the knee joint with metal and plastic parts.
treatments.knee-replacement.what: The worn surfaces of the thigh and shin bones are removed and capped with metal parts, with a plastic insert between them so the joint moves smoothly. Computer navigation or a robot may be used to position the parts precisely.
treatments.knee-replacement.who: People with severe knee pain and stiffness from arthritis that limits walking and sleep, when medicines, injections and physiotherapy no longer help.
treatments.knee-replacement.stay: About 6 days for one knee (1 in intensive care, 5 on the ward), or 8 days for both (2 and 6) at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.knee-replacement.recovery: Walking with support starts the day after surgery. Most people walk on their own in 4 to 6 weeks and fly home after about 2 to 3 weeks.
treatments.knee-replacement.faq.0.questi: Can both knees be done together?
treatments.knee-replacement.faq.0.answer: Often, yes, if your health allows. It means one stay and one recovery.
treatments.knee-replacement.faq.1.questi: How long does a knee replacement last?
treatments.knee-replacement.faq.1.answer: Most last 15 to 20 years or more.
treatments.hip-replacement.name: Total hip replacement
treatments.hip-replacement.summary: An operation that replaces a damaged hip joint with an artificial ball and socket.
treatments.hip-replacement.what: The worn ball at the top of the thigh bone and the socket in the pelvis are replaced with artificial parts made of metal, ceramic or plastic.
treatments.hip-replacement.who: People with severe hip pain and stiffness from arthritis, a hip fracture, or loss of blood supply to the hip bone (avascular necrosis).
treatments.hip-replacement.stay: About 6 days for one hip (1 in intensive care, 5 on the ward), or 8 days for both (2 and 6) at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.hip-replacement.recovery: Walking with support starts the day after surgery. Most people walk on their own in 4 to 6 weeks and fly home after about 2 weeks.
treatments.hip-replacement.faq.0.questio: How long does a hip replacement last?
treatments.hip-replacement.faq.0.answer: Most last 15 to 20 years or more.
treatments.hip-replacement.faq.1.questio: Are there movements I must avoid?
treatments.hip-replacement.faq.1.answer: For the first weeks, yes. The physiotherapist shows you how to sit, bend and climb stairs safely.
treatments.acl-reconstruction.name: ACL reconstruction
treatments.acl-reconstruction.summary: Keyhole surgery that rebuilds a torn anterior cruciate ligament, one of the main ligaments inside the knee.
treatments.acl-reconstruction.what: Through small cuts, the surgeon replaces the torn ligament with a piece of tendon, usually from the patient's own leg, fixed into the bones above and below the knee.
treatments.acl-reconstruction.who: Active people with a torn ACL whose knee gives way, especially those who play sport or do physical work.
treatments.acl-reconstruction.stay: Usually 1 to 2 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.acl-reconstruction.recovery: Walking with support starts within days. Return to sport usually takes 6 to 9 months of physiotherapy.
treatments.acl-reconstruction.faq.0.ques: Can I fly home soon after?
treatments.acl-reconstruction.faq.0.answ: Usually after about 1 to 2 weeks, once the wound is checked and physiotherapy is under way.
treatments.acl-reconstruction.faq.1.ques: Can other knee damage be fixed at the same time?
treatments.acl-reconstruction.faq.1.answ: Yes. Torn cartilage (meniscus) is often repaired in the same operation.
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.name: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG)
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.summary: Heart bypass surgery: a blood vessel from elsewhere in the body is used to route blood around a narrowed or blocked artery of the heart.
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.what: A healthy blood vessel is taken from the chest, arm or leg and joined to the heart artery beyond the blockage, so blood flows around it. It can be done with the heart beating (off-pump) or with a heart-lung machine, and in some patients through smaller cuts.
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.who: People with several blocked heart arteries, a blocked main artery, or diabetes with heart artery disease, and those for whom stenting is not suitable.
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.stay: About 7 to 9 days: 3 to 5 in intensive care, depending on risk, and 4 on the ward at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.recovery: Most people return to light activity in 4 to 6 weeks and full activity in about 3 months. Plan to stay in India for about 2 to 3 weeks after surgery.
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.faq.0.qu: Bypass or stent: which is better for me?
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.faq.0.an: It depends on how many arteries are blocked and where. The heart team reviews your angiogram and advises.
treatments.heart-bypass-surgery.faq.1.an: Usually about 2 to 3 weeks after surgery, after a check-up.
treatments.minimally-invasive-heart-surg: Heart surgery through small cuts between the ribs instead of opening the breastbone.

The surgeon reaches the heart through a small cut in the side of the chest, using special instruments and sometimes a camera. It can be used for valve repair or replacement, some bypass operations and closing holes in the heart.
Selected people needing valve, bypass or other heart surgery, depending on their heart and general health.
Usually 4 to 6 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
Often quicker than standard heart surgery: many return to light activity in 2 to 4 weeks.
No. It depends on the operation and your heart. The surgeon advises after reviewing your tests.
Is the result the same as standard surgery?
For suitable patients, yes, with a smaller scar and usually a faster recovery.
treatments.heart-valve-replacement.name: Heart valve replacement
treatments.heart-valve-replacement.summa: An operation or catheter procedure that replaces a heart valve that is too narrow or leaks, with a mechanical or tissue valve.
treatments.heart-valve-replacement.what: The faulty valve is repaired where possible, or replaced with a mechanical valve (which lasts very long but needs blood thinners for life) or a tissue valve. Some patients can have a new valve placed through a tube in the leg (TAVI) instead of open surgery.
treatments.heart-valve-replacement.who: People with a narrowed or leaking heart valve causing breathlessness, chest pain, tiredness or fainting, often after rheumatic fever or from age.
treatments.heart-valve-replacement.stay: About 7 days for one valve: 3 in intensive care and 4 on the ward at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.heart-valve-replacement.recov: Usually 6 to 8 weeks for open surgery, less with minimally invasive or catheter methods. Plan to stay in India for about 2 to 3 weeks.
treatments.heart-valve-replacement.faq.0: Mechanical valves last longer but need daily blood thinners. Tissue valves avoid this but may wear out after 10 to 20 years. The surgeon helps you choose.
treatments.heart-valve-replacement.faq.1: Can my valve be repaired instead?
Often, especially leaking mitral valves. Repair is preferred where possible.
treatments.angioplasty.name: Coronary angioplasty and stenting
treatments.angioplasty.summary: A thin tube is passed to a narrowed heart artery, a small balloon widens it, and a mesh tube called a stent is usually left to hold it open.
treatments.angioplasty.what: Through a pinhole in the wrist or groin, a thin tube is guided to the heart. An angiogram shows the blockage, a balloon opens it, and a stent coated with medicine is left in place to keep it open.
treatments.angioplasty.who: People with chest pain or a heart attack caused by one or a few narrowed heart arteries.
treatments.angioplasty.stay: About 2 days: 1 in intensive care and 1 on the ward at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.angioplasty.recovery: Most people return to normal activity in about a week, and can usually fly home after a few days.
treatments.angioplasty.faq.0.question: Is it done under general anaesthetic?
treatments.angioplasty.faq.0.answer: No. It is done under local anaesthetic, and you are awake but comfortable.
treatments.angioplasty.faq.1.question: Will I need medicines afterwards?
treatments.angioplasty.faq.1.answer: Yes, blood thinners for some months to protect the stent, and medicines to protect the heart.
treatments.ecmo.name: ECMO (heart and lung support)
treatments.ecmo.summary: A machine takes over the work of the heart and lungs for days or weeks, to give them time to recover.
treatments.ecmo.what: Blood is drawn through a tube, passed through an artificial lung that adds oxygen and removes carbon dioxide, and pumped back. It is used in intensive care for the most serious heart or lung failure, or to support complex heart surgery.
treatments.ecmo.who: Critically ill people with severe heart or lung failure that does not respond to other treatment, for example after a heart attack, severe pneumonia or heart surgery.
treatments.ecmo.stay: In intensive care, for as long as support is needed, usually days to weeks.
treatments.ecmo.recovery: Depends on the illness that needed ECMO. The team explains each step to the family.
treatments.ecmo.faq.0.question: Can a patient be moved to India on ECMO?
treatments.ecmo.faq.0.answer: In some cases, with an air ambulance team. Contact us urgently and we check with the hospital.
treatments.ecmo.faq.1.question: Is ECMO a treatment in itself?
treatments.ecmo.faq.1.answer: It supports the body while the heart or lungs recover, or until another treatment, such as surgery, is possible.
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.name: Heart and diabetes care
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.summary: A specialist check and treatment plan for heart disease and diabetes together, aimed at preventing heart attacks and strokes.
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.what: A physician who treats both conditions reviews your history, tests and medicines, and plans treatment for blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol together. Tests may include an ECG, echo, stress test and blood tests.
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.who: People with diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol or a family history of heart disease, and those who want a full heart check during their visit.
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.stay: No hospital stay: tests and consultations are done as an outpatient, usually over 1 to 2 days.
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.recovery: No recovery time. The plan can continue with your doctor at home.
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.faq.0.que: Can I have a heart check while I am in India for something else?
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.faq.0.ans: Yes. We can book it alongside your other appointments.
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.faq.1.que: Will I need to change my medicines?
treatments.heart-diabetes-care.faq.1.ans: Possibly. The doctor explains any change and shares the plan with your home doctor.
treatments.varicose-veins.name: Varicose vein treatment
treatments.varicose-veins.summary: Bulging, painful leg veins closed from the inside with heat or medicine, through a pinhole, without open surgery.
treatments.varicose-veins.what: Guided by ultrasound, a thin tube is passed into the faulty vein and heat (laser or radiofrequency) or a medical glue closes it. Blood then flows through healthy veins. Smaller veins can be treated with injections. Deep vein clots (DVT) can also be treated through a catheter.
treatments.varicose-veins.who: People with varicose veins causing pain, swelling, skin changes or ulcers, and some people with deep vein thrombosis.
treatments.varicose-veins.stay: Usually a day procedure, or 1 night in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.varicose-veins.recovery: Most people walk straight away and return to normal activity in a few days, wearing a support stocking for a week or two.
treatments.varicose-veins.faq.0.question: Is it painful?
treatments.varicose-veins.faq.0.answer: It is done under local anaesthetic. Mild aching for a few days is common.
treatments.varicose-veins.faq.1.question: Can the veins come back?
treatments.varicose-veins.faq.1.answer: New varicose veins can form over the years, and can be treated again.
treatments.peripheral-artery-disease.sum: Narrowed or blocked arteries in the legs opened with a balloon or stent through a pinhole, to ease pain on walking and save the leg.
treatments.peripheral-artery-disease.wha: Through a pinhole, an interventional radiologist guides a thin tube to the blocked artery, opens it with a balloon, and may place a stent. Where this is not possible, a bypass operation may be advised.
treatments.peripheral-artery-disease.who: People with leg pain on walking, pain at rest, or wounds that do not heal because of poor blood flow, often with diabetes or a history of smoking.
treatments.peripheral-artery-disease.sta: Usually 1 to 2 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.peripheral-artery-disease.rec: Most people walk the same or next day and return to normal activity within a week.
treatments.peripheral-artery-disease.faq: Restoring blood flow can help wounds heal and often saves the leg. The earlier it is treated, the better.
Yes, usually blood thinners and cholesterol medicines, and help to stop smoking.
treatments.hand-surgery.name: Hand surgery and reconstruction
treatments.hand-surgery.summary: Surgery to repair injured or damaged hands and restore their use, from cut tendons and nerves to reattaching fingers.
treatments.hand-surgery.what: A hand surgeon repairs tendons, nerves, blood vessels and bones under a microscope, reattaches severed fingers, frees stiff or contracted fingers, and rebuilds missing parts with tissue moved from elsewhere. Hand therapy afterwards is a key part of recovery.
treatments.hand-surgery.who: People with hand injuries, nerve compression such as carpal tunnel syndrome, stiff or bent fingers, birth differences of the hand, or poor hand function after an old injury.
treatments.hand-surgery.stay: Usually a day procedure to 3 days in hospital, depending on the operation. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.hand-surgery.recovery: From 2 weeks for minor surgery to several months with hand therapy for complex repairs.
treatments.hand-surgery.faq.0.question: Can an old injury still be improved?
treatments.hand-surgery.faq.0.answer: Often, yes. Tendon and nerve transfers can bring back movement years after an injury.
treatments.hand-surgery.faq.1.question: Do I need hand therapy?
treatments.hand-surgery.faq.1.answer: Yes. Therapy is as important as the operation for getting movement back.
treatments.brachial-plexus-surgery.name: Brachial plexus and nerve surgery
treatments.brachial-plexus-surgery.summa: Surgery to repair the nerves from the neck to the arm, after injury or at birth, to bring back movement to the shoulder, arm and hand.
treatments.brachial-plexus-surgery.what: The brachial plexus is the bundle of nerves that controls the arm. Under a microscope, the surgeon repairs damaged nerves, uses nerve grafts, or moves working nerves or muscles to restore movement. Timing matters: nerves recover best when repaired within months of the injury.
treatments.brachial-plexus-surgery.who: Adults with arm weakness or paralysis after a road accident or fall, and babies with arm weakness from a difficult birth (birth brachial plexus palsy).
treatments.brachial-plexus-surgery.stay: Usually 3 to 5 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
