treatments.brachial-plexus-surgery.recov: Nerves grow slowly, so movement returns over 6 months to 2 years, with long-term physiotherapy.
treatments.brachial-plexus-surgery.faq.0: Is it too late if the injury was a year ago?
Not always. Even when nerve repair is no longer possible, nerve or muscle transfers can still help.
treatments.brachial-plexus-surgery.faq.1: When should a baby be seen?
As early as possible, ideally within the first few months, so the surgeon can follow recovery and operate at the right time.
treatments.reconstructive-microsurgery.s: Rebuilding parts of the body after injury or cancer surgery by moving tissue, with its blood supply, from elsewhere in the body.
treatments.reconstructive-microsurgery.w: Skin, muscle or bone is moved from one part of the body to another, and its tiny blood vessels are joined under a microscope so it survives. It is used to cover wounds, rebuild the face, breast or jaw after cancer surgery, and save severely injured legs that might otherwise be amputated.
People with large wounds or missing tissue after accidents, burns, infections or cancer surgery, including severe leg injuries.
treatments.reconstructive-microsurgery.s: Usually 5 to 10 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.reconstructive-microsurgery.r: Usually 4 to 8 weeks, longer for leg reconstruction, with physiotherapy.
treatments.reconstructive-microsurgery.f: Can my leg be saved after a bad injury?
Often, even after severe injuries. The team assesses the bone, skin and blood supply to decide.
Will there be a scar where the tissue is taken from?
Yes, but the surgeon chooses a place where it is least noticed and least affects function.
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.name: Lymphoedema surgery (lymphatic microsurgery)
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.summary: Microsurgery that helps fluid drain from a swollen arm or leg, often after cancer treatment.
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.what: Lymphoedema is swelling caused when lymph fluid cannot drain. Under a microscope, the surgeon joins tiny lymph vessels to small veins so fluid can drain (lymphovenous bypass), or moves healthy lymph nodes to the swollen limb.
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.who: People with arm or leg swelling from lymphoedema, often after breast or gynaecological cancer surgery or radiotherapy, when compression and therapy are not enough.
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.stay: Usually 1 to 3 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.recovery: Most people return to normal activity in 2 to 3 weeks. Swelling improves gradually over months, with continued compression.
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.faq.0.que: Will the swelling go away completely?
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.faq.0.ans: It usually improves, often a great deal, but may not disappear fully. Early treatment gives the best results.
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.faq.1.que: Do I still need compression garments?
treatments.lymphoedema-surgery.faq.1.ans: Usually yes for a while after surgery. Many people can wear them less over time.
treatments.childrens-plastic-surgery.nam: Plastic surgery for children and birth differences
treatments.childrens-plastic-surgery.sum: Surgery for children born with differences such as cleft lip and palate, hand differences and birthmarks, or with scars from injuries and burns.
treatments.childrens-plastic-surgery.wha: A plastic surgeon who operates on children repairs cleft lip and palate, separates joined fingers, corrects other hand and face differences, and releases tight burn scars, timed to suit the child's growth.
treatments.childrens-plastic-surgery.who: Babies and children with cleft lip or palate, hand or face differences from birth, birthmarks, or scars after injuries and burns.
treatments.childrens-plastic-surgery.sta: Usually 1 to 3 days in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.childrens-plastic-surgery.rec: Usually 1 to 3 weeks. Some conditions need more than one operation as the child grows.
treatments.childrens-plastic-surgery.faq: What is the best age for surgery?
It depends on the condition. A cleft lip is often repaired at around 3 to 6 months, a cleft palate before about 18 months.
Can a parent stay with the child?
Yes. A parent stays with the child in hospital throughout.
treatments.rhinoplasty.name: Rhinoplasty (nose reshaping)
treatments.rhinoplasty.summary: Surgery to change the shape or size of the nose, for appearance, for breathing, or both.
treatments.rhinoplasty.what: The surgeon reshapes the bone and cartilage of the nose, usually through cuts inside the nose or a small cut between the nostrils. A bent septum can be straightened in the same operation to help breathing.
treatments.rhinoplasty.who: Adults who want to change the shape of their nose, or who have breathing problems from a bent septum or past injury.
treatments.rhinoplasty.stay: Usually a day procedure or 1 night in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.rhinoplasty.recovery: A splint stays on for about a week. Most swelling and bruising settles in 2 weeks, and the final shape shows over months.
treatments.rhinoplasty.faq.0.question: When can I fly home?
treatments.rhinoplasty.faq.0.answer: Usually after about 7 to 10 days, once the splint is removed.
treatments.rhinoplasty.faq.1.question: Will it fix my breathing too?
treatments.rhinoplasty.faq.1.answer: If the problem is a bent septum, it can be corrected in the same operation.
treatments.liposuction.name: Liposuction
treatments.liposuction.summary: Surgery that removes fat from chosen areas of the body through small cuts. It reshapes the body; it is not a weight-loss treatment.
treatments.liposuction.what: Fat is loosened and removed through thin tubes inserted through small cuts, from areas such as the belly, thighs, arms or neck. A compression garment is worn afterwards to help the skin settle.
treatments.liposuction.who: Adults near a healthy weight with areas of fat that do not go with diet and exercise.
treatments.liposuction.stay: Usually a day procedure or 1 night in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.liposuction.recovery: Most people return to desk work in a week. Swelling settles over weeks to months.
treatments.liposuction.faq.0.question: Is it a way to lose weight?
treatments.liposuction.faq.0.answer: No. It reshapes the body. For large amounts of weight, weight loss surgery may be more suitable.
treatments.liposuction.faq.1.question: Will the fat come back?
treatments.liposuction.faq.1.answer: The removed fat cells do not return, but weight gain can add fat elsewhere.
treatments.hair-transplant.name: Hair transplant (FUE)
treatments.hair-transplant.summary: Hair follicles are moved one by one from the back or sides of the head to thinning or bald areas.
treatments.hair-transplant.what: Under local anaesthetic, healthy follicles are taken one by one from the back or sides of the head (follicular unit extraction) and placed in thinning areas. It takes most of a day.
treatments.hair-transplant.who: Men and women with pattern hair loss or thinning, who have enough healthy hair at the back and sides of the head.
treatments.hair-transplant.stay: No hospital stay: it is a day procedure.
treatments.hair-transplant.recovery: Most people return to normal activity in a few days. The new hair falls out at first and regrows over 3 to 12 months.
treatments.hair-transplant.faq.0.answer: New hair starts to grow in about 3 to 4 months, with the full result at about a year.
treatments.hair-transplant.faq.1.questio: Can I fly home the next day?
treatments.hair-transplant.faq.1.answer: Usually yes, after a check of the treated areas.
treatments.cataract-surgery.name: Cataract surgery with premium lens (IOL)
treatments.cataract-surgery.summary: The cloudy natural lens of the eye is removed and replaced with a clear artificial lens.
treatments.cataract-surgery.what: Through a tiny cut, the cloudy lens is broken up with ultrasound (phacoemulsification) or with help from a femtosecond laser, and a folded artificial lens (IOL) is put in its place. Premium lenses can also correct astigmatism or give clear sight at more than one distance. Each eye takes about 15 to 30 minutes, under numbing drops.
treatments.cataract-surgery.who: People whose cataract makes their sight cloudy, dim or glary enough to get in the way of daily life.
treatments.cataract-surgery.stay: No hospital stay: it is a day procedure. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.cataract-surgery.recovery: Most people see well within a few days and return to light daily life within a week. Plan to stay in India for about a week after the first eye; the second eye is often done a few days later.
treatments.cataract-surgery.faq.0.questi: Can both eyes be done on one trip?
treatments.cataract-surgery.faq.0.answer: Usually yes. The second eye is often done a few days to a week after the first, once the first eye has been checked.
treatments.cataract-surgery.faq.1.answer: It depends on the lens you choose. Premium lenses can reduce the need for glasses; the surgeon explains the options after measuring your eyes.
treatments.lasik.name: LASIK, Femto-LASIK and CLEAR laser vision correction
treatments.lasik.summary: A laser reshapes the clear front of the eye (the cornea) so that glasses or contact lenses are no longer needed.
treatments.lasik.what: The cornea is reshaped with a laser so light focuses correctly on the retina. In LASIK and bladeless Femto-LASIK a thin flap is lifted before the laser works; in CLEAR, a small piece of tissue is removed through a tiny keyhole without a flap. Both eyes are usually treated in the same session, which takes about 15 to 30 minutes, under numbing drops.
treatments.lasik.who: Adults over 18 whose glasses power has been stable for at least a year, with healthy eyes and a cornea thick enough for the treatment. Detailed scans decide which method suits you.
treatments.lasik.stay: No hospital stay: it is a day procedure. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.lasik.recovery: Most people see clearly within a day or two and return to work in a few days. Plan to stay in India for about a week for the follow-up checks.
treatments.lasik.faq.0.question: Is it painful?
treatments.lasik.faq.0.answer: No. Numbing drops are used, and most people feel only light pressure. The eyes may feel gritty for a day or so afterwards.
treatments.lasik.faq.1.question: How do I know which laser method is right for me?
treatments.lasik.faq.1.answer: The surgeon decides after scans of your cornea. Your reports from home help us give you a first opinion before you travel.
treatments.icl.name: Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL)
treatments.icl.summary: A thin lens is placed inside the eye to correct high glasses power, for people who cannot have laser treatment.
treatments.icl.what: Through a tiny cut, a soft, thin lens is placed inside the eye in front of the natural lens. The natural lens is kept, and the ICL can be removed later if needed. Each eye takes about 20 to 30 minutes, under numbing drops.
treatments.icl.who: Adults with high short-sight or astigmatism, or a cornea that is too thin for LASIK.
treatments.icl.stay: No hospital stay: it is a day procedure. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.icl.recovery: Sight usually improves within a day or two. Plan to stay in India for about a week for checks.
treatments.icl.faq.0.question: Can I feel the lens in my eye?
treatments.icl.faq.0.answer: No. The lens sits inside the eye and cannot be felt once it is in place.
treatments.keratoconus-treatment.name: Keratoconus treatment (corneal cross-linking)
treatments.keratoconus-treatment.summary: Treatment that stops a thinning, cone-shaped cornea from getting worse, and helps sight with special lenses.
treatments.keratoconus-treatment.what: In corneal cross-linking, vitamin B2 (riboflavin) drops are put on the eye and then a measured ultraviolet light is shone on it. This strengthens the cornea and stops the cone from getting steeper. Special contact lenses or a lens implant may then improve sight.
treatments.keratoconus-treatment.who: Children and adults whose keratoconus is getting worse, seen on repeat corneal scans.
treatments.keratoconus-treatment.stay: No hospital stay: it is a day procedure. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.keratoconus-treatment.recover: The eye is sore for a few days while the surface heals. Plan to stay in India for about a week for checks.
treatments.keratoconus-treatment.faq.0.q: Will cross-linking bring back my sight?
treatments.keratoconus-treatment.faq.0.a: Its main aim is to stop keratoconus from getting worse. Sight is then helped with lenses; the doctor explains what to expect for your eye.
treatments.corneal-transplant.name: Corneal transplant (keratoplasty)
treatments.corneal-transplant.summary: A damaged or scarred cornea is replaced, in full or in layers, with healthy donor tissue.
treatments.corneal-transplant.what: The damaged part of the cornea is removed and replaced with clear tissue from a donor eye. Depending on the problem, the whole thickness is replaced or only the front or back layers. Donor tissue comes from an approved eye bank.
treatments.corneal-transplant.who: People with a scarred, cloudy or badly misshapen cornea, for example from infection, injury or advanced keratoconus.
treatments.corneal-transplant.stay: Usually a day procedure or one night in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.corneal-transplant.recovery: Sight improves slowly over months. Plan to stay in India for about 2 to 3 weeks for close checks, and to use eye drops for a long time afterwards.
treatments.corneal-transplant.faq.0.ques: Where does the donor cornea come from?
treatments.corneal-transplant.faq.0.answ: From an eye bank. Corneal transplants in India can only be done at hospitals approved for them under Indian law.
treatments.glaucoma-treatment.name: Glaucoma treatment
treatments.glaucoma-treatment.summary: Drops, laser or surgery to lower the pressure inside the eye and protect sight from glaucoma.
treatments.glaucoma-treatment.what: Glaucoma slowly damages the nerve at the back of the eye, usually because the pressure inside the eye is too high. Treatment lowers the pressure: first with eye drops, then with laser, and if needed with surgery that makes a new drainage path for the fluid in the eye.
treatments.glaucoma-treatment.who: People diagnosed with glaucoma, or with high eye pressure that puts their sight at risk.
treatments.glaucoma-treatment.stay: No hospital stay for laser; a day procedure or one night for surgery. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.glaucoma-treatment.recovery: Laser needs only a short rest. After surgery, plan to stay in India for about 2 weeks for checks.
treatments.glaucoma-treatment.faq.0.answ: No. Sight already lost cannot be brought back, which is why treatment aims to protect the sight that remains.
treatments.vitreoretinal-surgery.name: Retina and vitreo-retinal surgery
treatments.vitreoretinal-surgery.summary: Laser, injections or surgery for problems at the back of the eye, such as retinal detachment or diabetic eye disease.
treatments.vitreoretinal-surgery.what: Depending on the problem, the retina is treated with laser, with injections into the eye, or with vitrectomy: the gel inside the eye is removed so the surgeon can repair the retina. A detached retina is put back in place and held with gas or oil.
treatments.vitreoretinal-surgery.who: People with a detached or torn retina, bleeding inside the eye, diabetic eye disease, a macular hole or age-related macular degeneration.
treatments.vitreoretinal-surgery.stay: Usually a day procedure; sometimes one night in hospital. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.vitreoretinal-surgery.recover: Recovery depends on the operation. After vitrectomy you may need to hold your head in one position for some days, and you cannot fly while there is gas in the eye. Plan to stay in India for about 2 to 3 weeks.
treatments.vitreoretinal-surgery.faq.0.a: Not while a gas bubble is in the eye, which can take a few weeks. The surgeon tells you when it is safe.
treatments.squint-surgery.name: Squint surgery and children's eye care
treatments.squint-surgery.summary: Surgery on the eye muscles to straighten eyes that turn in, out, up or down, for children and adults.
treatments.squint-surgery.what: The muscles that move the eye are tightened or loosened so the eyes line up. Children also have their sight checked for lazy eye and glasses before any surgery is planned.
treatments.squint-surgery.who: Children and adults with a squint that glasses or exercises have not corrected.
treatments.squint-surgery.stay: No hospital stay: it is a day procedure. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.squint-surgery.recovery: The eye is red and sore for a week or two. Plan to stay in India for about a week.
treatments.squint-surgery.faq.0.question: Is the operation done under general anaesthetic?
treatments.squint-surgery.faq.0.answer: For children, usually yes. Adults can sometimes have it under local anaesthetic.
treatments.oculoplastic-surgery.name: Oculoplastic surgery
treatments.oculoplastic-surgery.summary: Surgery for the eyelids, tear ducts and the bones around the eye.
treatments.oculoplastic-surgery.what: Operations on the eyelids (such as a droopy lid or an eyelid that turns in or out), the tear drainage system (such as a blocked tear duct) and the eye socket, including removal of growths and reconstruction after injury.
treatments.oculoplastic-surgery.who: People with eyelid, tear duct or eye socket problems, for medical or cosmetic reasons.
treatments.oculoplastic-surgery.stay: Usually a day procedure. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.oculoplastic-surgery.recovery: Swelling and bruising settle over 1 to 2 weeks. Plan to stay in India for about a week to 10 days, until stitches are removed.
treatments.oculoplastic-surgery.faq.0.qu: Will there be a visible scar?
treatments.oculoplastic-surgery.faq.0.an: Cuts are usually hidden in the natural creases of the eyelid, so scars are hard to see once healed.
treatments.dental-implants.name: Dental implants
treatments.dental-implants.summary: A titanium post is placed in the jaw to hold a new tooth where one is missing.
treatments.dental-implants.what: A small titanium post is placed in the jawbone under local anaesthetic. Once the bone has grown around it, a crown, bridge or denture is fixed on top. Some cases allow a temporary tooth on the same day.
treatments.dental-implants.who: Adults with one or more missing teeth and enough healthy jawbone, or who can have a bone graft first.
treatments.dental-implants.stay: No hospital stay: each visit is a clinic appointment. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.dental-implants.recovery: Most people return to normal life the next day. The bone takes about 3 to 6 months to heal around the implant, so treatment is often split over two trips, unless the dentist can fit the final tooth sooner.
treatments.dental-implants.faq.0.questio: Can it be done in one trip?
treatments.dental-implants.faq.0.answer: Sometimes. It depends on your bone and the type of implant. The dentist tells you after seeing your X-rays.
treatments.root-canal-treatment.name: Root canal treatment
treatments.root-canal-treatment.summary: The infected inside of a tooth is cleaned and sealed, so the tooth can be kept instead of pulled out.
treatments.root-canal-treatment.what: Under local anaesthetic, the infected or damaged pulp inside the tooth is removed, the canals are cleaned and shaped, and then filled and sealed. A crown is often placed afterwards to protect the tooth.
treatments.root-canal-treatment.who: People with a badly decayed, cracked or infected tooth that causes pain or swelling.
treatments.root-canal-treatment.stay: No hospital stay: usually 1 to 3 clinic visits. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.root-canal-treatment.recovery: The tooth may be tender for a few days. Most people go back to normal eating within a week.
treatments.root-canal-treatment.faq.0.an: It is done under local anaesthetic, so it should feel much like a normal filling.
treatments.smile-design.name: Smile design and cosmetic dentistry
treatments.smile-design.summary: Veneers, whitening and tooth-coloured fillings to improve the look of your smile.
treatments.smile-design.what: The dentist plans the shape, size and colour of your teeth, then uses veneers or laminates, whitening, tooth-coloured fillings or crowns to reach that look.
treatments.smile-design.who: People who want to change stained, chipped, uneven or gapped teeth.
treatments.smile-design.stay: No hospital stay: usually a few clinic visits over 1 to 2 weeks. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.smile-design.recovery: No recovery time for most treatments. Teeth may feel sensitive for a few days.
treatments.smile-design.faq.0.question: How long do veneers last?
treatments.smile-design.faq.0.answer: Porcelain veneers usually last 10 years or more with good care.
treatments.full-mouth-rehabilitation.sum: A planned set of treatments that rebuilds all the teeth when many are worn, broken or missing.
treatments.full-mouth-rehabilitation.wha: A mix of crowns, bridges, implants, root canal treatment and gum care is planned together to rebuild the bite and the look of the teeth.
treatments.full-mouth-rehabilitation.who: People with many damaged or missing teeth, a worn-down bite, or problems from several old treatments.
treatments.full-mouth-rehabilitation.sta: No hospital stay: a series of clinic visits. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.full-mouth-rehabilitation.rec: It depends on the plan. Some work can be done in one trip of 1 to 2 weeks; plans with implants may need a second trip.
treatments.full-mouth-rehabilitation.faq: How many trips will I need?
The dentist sets the plan after seeing your X-rays and tells you how many visits are needed.
treatments.braces-aligners.name: Braces and clear aligners
treatments.braces-aligners.summary: Braces or clear aligners that slowly move teeth into a straighter position.
treatments.braces-aligners.what: Fixed braces or removable clear aligners apply gentle pressure to move teeth over months. The dentist takes scans or moulds and plans each step.
treatments.braces-aligners.who: Children and adults with crooked, crowded or gapped teeth, or a bite that does not meet properly.
treatments.braces-aligners.stay: No hospital stay: clinic visits. Your hospital confirms it for your case.
treatments.braces-aligners.recovery: Treatment usually takes 6 to 24 months. With aligners, most checks can be done from home after the first visit.
treatments.braces-aligners.faq.0.questio: Can I be treated if I live abroad?
treatments.braces-aligners.faq.0.answer: Often yes with clear aligners: the first visit is in person, and later sets of aligners can be sent to you.

posts.bilateral-hand-transplant-nanavati: A double hand transplant gives an 18-year-old his hands back
A young farmer who lost both hands in an accident received two donor hands in a 13-hour operation at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital, Mumbai.
In January 2024, an 18-year-old farmer's son from Gujarat lost both hands in an accident with farm machinery. The crush injury was too severe to repair, and both hands had to be amputated.
After detailed medical, psychological and immune testing, doctors judged that he was suitable for a transplant of both hands. Donor hands are rare and have to match closely, so he waited 13 months.

In January 2026 the family of a 50-year-old woman who had died in Surat agreed to donate her organs. Her lungs, liver and corneas went to patients in Mumbai and Surat, and her hands to him. Teams in Gujarat and Maharashtra worked together to bring the hands to Mumbai in the short time available.

The operation took place overnight on 9 to 10 January 2026, led by Dr Nilesh Satbhai, Director of Plastic, Reconstructive Microsurgery and Hand Transplantation. Over 13 hours the team fixed the bones, joined the arteries and veins, repaired the tendons, connected the nerves and closed the skin. Blood flowed into both hands as soon as the vessels were joined.

Afterwards he was cared for by a team that managed medicine to stop rejection, watched the blood supply closely, prevented infection and started rehabilitation early. It was the first bilateral hand transplant at Nanavati Max.

A hand transplant is harder than an organ transplant, because it moves skin, muscle, tendon, bone, vessels and nerves together, and skin is very likely to be rejected. When it works, it can bring back feeling and coordinated movement that a prosthetic hand cannot.
If you or someone in your family has lost a hand or arm, send us the medical reports. A specialist will tell you whether a transplant or reconstruction could help.

posts.thumb-reconstruction-toddler-nanav: Born without a thumb: how surgeons rebuilt a toddler's grip
A baby girl born with severe thumb deformities on both hands can now grip and hold, after two operations at Nanavati Max Super Speciality Hospital, Mumbai.
A little girl was born without a left thumb, and with a right thumb too underdeveloped to use. Without working thumbs, a child struggles to learn to grasp, pinch and hold things.

Dr Nilesh G Satbhai, Director of Plastic, Reconstructive Microsurgery and Hand Transplantation, and his team planned two operations. Her blood vessels and nerves were tiny, which made the work delicate, and because both hands were affected, both operations had to succeed.
The first operation, in December 2025, steadied the weak right thumb and moved a muscle from her palm so the thumb could turn and touch the other fingers. Within weeks she began to use it.

The second, in February 2026, built a new left thumb by moving the second toe from her left foot to her hand and joining its blood vessels, nerves and tendons under the microscope. The surgeons also rebuilt the foot so it would keep working normally.
At 13 months old she can hold her parents' fingers. Surgery like this works best early, while a child is still learning to use their hands.
If your child was born with a hand difference, send us photos and any reports. A specialist will advise what can be done and when.
